summary: Enhanced ARPA/IRA ACA premium subsidies EXPIRED 2025-12-31 and NOTHING has been enacted to restore them. 2026 prices on the pre-ARPA regime: the 400% FPL cliff is back and the contribution percentages are higher. Re-verified 2026-07-26 against the statute itself plus a full-text sweep of every 2026 public law — over-determined, not a news read. The House bill is PARKED, not defeated (see pendingExtension), and any later enactment WOULD be retroactive to all of 2026 by its own drafted effective date.
discriminatingProof: 26 U.S.C. 36B(b)(3)(A)(iii) 'Temporary percentages for 2021 through 2025' and 36B(c)(1)(E) 'Temporary rule for 2021 through 2025' BOTH read 'before January 1, 2026' — the enhanced table and the cliff removal are expired on the face of the statute (uscode.house.gov prelim, granule currency marker currentthrough:20260413_119-83).

Rev. Proc. 2025-25 §3.01 (the 2026 table the engine prices): the band list TERMINATES at 'At least 300% but not more than 400% — 9.96%' with NO row above 400%, and its floor band is 2.10%. ARPA §9661(a) set that floor to 0.00% and capped the top at 8.5%; §9661(b) removed the 400% ceiling entirely. The shape of this table IS the reversion.

AFFIRMATIVE, IN-WINDOW: Rev. Proc. 2026-26 (IRB 2026-31, 2026-07-27, p.131) publishes the TY2027 table in the SAME reverted shape — floor 2.15%, terminating at 'At least 300% but not more than 400% — 10.22%', Required Contribution Percentage 10.22%. Treasury could not have published that shape if the enhanced schedule had been restored. This is evidence of the status, not merely absence of contrary news.

pendingExtension: H.R. 1834 ('Breaking the Gridlock Act' — a shell vehicle; the ACA substance arrived by McGovern substitute, so a purpose-named health bill will not be found) passed the House 2026-01-08, 230-196 (Roll 11), and has sat on Senate Legislative Calendar No. 319 since 2026-02-10 with NO floor action. THE SENATE HAS NEVER VOTED ON IT. The S. 3385 cloture failure (51-48, Record Vote 644) was 2025-12-11 — it PREDATES the House bill by four weeks and is NOT the Senate's answer to it. Posture: parked-and-available, which is the shape that gets attached to a funding vehicle — not spent.
retroactivity: DRAFTED IN, not merely possible. H.R. 1834 §1(c): 'The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.' Enactment on ANY 2026 date restores all twelve months, reconciled on Form 8962 at filing. CONDITION the tool must not omit: §36B(c)(2)(A) requires a coverage month in which the premium was actually PAID — a household that drops Marketplace coverage in 2026 because the unsubsidized price is unaffordable recovers NOTHING from a later restoration.
adjacentButSharp: Pub. L. 119-21 §71305 struck §36B(f)(2)(B), REMOVING the excess-APTC repayment cap for tax years beginning after 2025-12-31. It does not change the credit formula the engine models (the overlay prices from actual-year MAGI; there is no advance/reconcile split). It DOES remove the ceiling on the downside of a mis-estimated year — which lands directly on a recommendation that sizes a conversion near the cliff. Neither pending bill restores the cap: both amend only (b)(3)(A)(iii) and (c)(1)(E). Do not file this as merely 'adjacent'.

howToClear: Re-verify the CURRENT ACA enhanced-subsidy status against an enacted statute / IRS notice, then update verifiedOn + status + summary. Do NOT just bump the date — the law can flip the whole pre-65 model. THE CHAIN THAT WORKS (each link independent): (1) read §36B(b)(3)(A)(iii) and (c)(1)(E) at uscode.house.gov and note the granule's currentthrough marker; (2) full-text sweep every public law ABOVE that marker from govinfo, checking BODIES not status codes; (3) confirm the law ceiling the same way; (4) check congress.gov presented-to-president.xml is empty; (5) find the newest Rev. Proc. applicable-percentage table and confirm whether it terminates at 400%. Step 5 is affirmative evidence and is worth more than any number of absent-news searches.
